nodes.tried: Staging at e9fdde3 on the code defaults (d353282 / 1a67f1a), with every Vertex request held >= 1.0 s apart (appeal commitment), against a same-session arm with both flags off.
nodes.broke: Replies got slower, not faster: v2-flashlite p50 3,201 vs 2,301 ms, v2-mai 2,658 vs 2,054 ms (n=22-23 each). The pacer queues the confirmed brain request behind discarded speculative requests (24 and 28 waits per 4 calls, 12-15 s in all) and warm HEADs. Speculation kept its reply in only 2 of about 23 replies, and the defaults sent 1.5-2.0x the Vertex requests. Not a verdict on the flags without a pacer, which was not measured here.

nodes.broke: The runtime's judge sends a static key, and a Vertex token lasts about an hour, after which every judge call would be judge_unavailable:error. It works only for a bounded batch with a token minted at restart. Left off. The fix is for the voice runtime: mint the judge's token from the service account as GoogleRoute's VertexToken does for brain and voice.

nodes.title: Choosing the judge threshold as 'the lowest DEV sweep threshold with judge FP <= 5%' for a model whose confidences come in steps
nodes.tried: PREREG.md for BLIND 8: the lowest threshold on 0.3-0.9 with DEV judge FP <= 5%, else the fewest FP at recall >= 95%, else 0.5.
nodes.broke: Flash-Lite's DEV confidences are step-quantised (0.85, 0.95, 1.0). 6 of its 8 false positives and 24 true crisis verdicts sit at exactly 0.85, so the only qualifying value was 0.9 (DEV judge recall 88 -> 60/100). On BLIND 8 it gave judge recall 73/100, where the information-only sweep shows 93/100 at 0.5 with 1/100 FP. A next rule should choose by recall under an FP bound with a CI, or handle tied confidence steps explicitly. BLIND 8 is not re-scored.
